title: Compliance layer contract v1.0.0
description: Phase 6. Four tables under data/gold/compliance/. `leads` carries one row per fixture-derived lead in the shape of contracts/lead_output.schema.json (which is NOT modified and is validated against separately, row by row, with jsonschema format checking on) plus the provenance columns a warehouse needs and a downstream consumer does not. `decision_lineage` is append-only and content-addressed. `crash_only_decisions` is the production-truth table -- every gold crash evaluated with no identity layer, which is the memo's answer to the per-jurisdiction lawfulness question. `exclusion_by_code` is the exclusion table itself, over both runs. Same dialect as bronze/silver/gold/analysis: typed properties, x-column-order-is-contract, unique_keys, and row_rules for the cross-column invariants JSON Schema cannot express.

compliance.leads.title: One row per lead, with a complete eligibility decision
compliance.leads.description: The grain is the PARTY, not the crash: fixtures/synthetic_parties.csv has no key into gold, so each fixture row becomes exactly one lead whether or not a crash could be matched to it. `geo`, `contact` and `consent` are STRUCT columns here and JSON-encoded strings in output/sample_leads.csv; both round-trip to the same object, and the CSV validator re-parses each cell before jsonschema.validate. No column carries a name, a street, a city, an E.164 number or a coordinate -- the boundary is drawn in src/compliance/vault.py and 18 U.S.C. 2725(3) is why the finest DIRECT location here is zip5.

row_rules.name: reason_codes_non_empty
row_rules.description: contracts/lead_output.schema.json says minItems: 1. A record with no codes is a record with no reasoning, and the default disposition is emitted as NO_AFFIRMATIVE_BASIS rather than as an absence.

row_rules.name: legal_basis_parallel_to_reason_codes
row_rules.description: The two arrays are emitted parallel -- one citation per code, same order -- because the contract has them as separate arrays and a consumer has no other way to pair them. A shorter legal_basis is an uncited exclusion.

row_rules.name: blocked_until_has_a_future_date
row_rules.predicate: eligibility_status <> 'BLOCKED_UNTIL' OR (blocked_until_date IS NOT NULL AND blocked_until_date > CAST(evaluated_at AS DATE))
row_rules.description: BLOCKED_UNTIL must carry a date, and that date must be after the evaluation date -- a window that has already opened is not a block. Written against evaluated_at rather than a literal as_of so the rule holds for any run date; evaluated_at IS as_of at 00:00 UTC by construction (see src/compliance/engine.py).

row_rules.name: eligible_requires_affirmative_code
row_rules.description: ASSIGNMENT.md Part 5: eligibility must be affirmatively proven, per record, with a citation. An ELIGIBLE row whose codes contain no affirmative basis has not proven anything, and this is the rule that refuses to ship it.

row_rules.name: ineligible_publishes_no_date
row_rules.description: A date on an INELIGIBLE record would tell the business it becomes contactable then, which is false: the failure is either non-curable or curable by a refresh, and neither is cleared by the passage of time.

row_rules.name: matched_lead_has_a_crash
row_rules.description: match_method and crash_sk say the same thing and must never disagree. A NO_MATCH row with a crash_sk would mean a crash was attached without a recorded method.

row_rules.name: unmatched_lead_is_source_other
row_rules.description: No matched crash means no source system to claim. Attributing an unmatched lead to MONTGOMERY_MD would be fabricating a provenance, which is the one thing Part 5 says a record may never do.

compliance.decision_lineage.title: Immutable, append-only decision audit records
compliance.decision_lineage.description: One row per distinct decision. `decision_lineage_id` is sha256(tokenised input, ruleset sha, blackout sha, as_of), so a re-run appends nothing and any change appends a NEW row rather than updating one. The row CONTAINS the state that produced the decision -- ordered findings with params as evaluated, citations as they read on the day, the tokenised input snapshot -- because eighteen months from now rules.yaml will say something else.

row_rules.name: lineage_reason_codes_non_empty
row_rules.description: Codes are pipe-joined here rather than a LIST because a lineage row is read as text by a human reconstructing a decision, and a pipe-joined string survives a CSV export intact.

row_rules.name: lineage_snapshot_is_json
row_rules.description: An audit record that cannot be parsed is not an audit record. Checked here rather than trusted because these three columns are the only place the state that produced a decision survives.

row_rules.name: lineage_blocked_until_matches_status
row_rules.description: The lineage row must agree with the lead row it explains: a date exactly when the status is BLOCKED_UNTIL, never otherwise.

compliance.crash_only_decisions.title: Production truth: every gold crash evaluated with NO identity layer
compliance.crash_only_decisions.description: The table that answers ASSIGNMENT.md Part 7's direct question. A gold crash has a jurisdiction, dates and geography and no contact block at all, so it enters the same engine as PUBLIC_CRASH_REPORT provenance with no phone, no consent and no line type. What comes out is the honest count of deliverable leads from the real sources -- and the honest count is expected to be zero in every jurisdiction, which is a passing answer and is the one the memo states.

row_rules.name: crash_only_is_never_eligible_without_proof
row_rules.description: Same affirmative-basis rule as the lead table. If this ever fires it means the engine found a permissible use in a record that has no contact details at all, which would be a bug worth stopping the build for.

compliance.exclusion_by_code.title: The exclusion table the memo asks for
compliance.exclusion_by_code.description: Counts by run x jurisdiction x eligibility_status x reason_code, over BOTH the fixture leads and the crash-only run. ASSIGNMENT.md Part 7: 'We want the exclusion table. It is more informative than the inclusion table.' `disposition` carries what the code MEANS under the ruleset that produced the count, so a reader does not have to hold rules.yaml open beside it.

row_rules.name: eligible_carries_no_blocking_code
row_rules.description: An ELIGIBLE record may carry an affirmative basis and a NOTE (a VoIP number routed to the wireless tier is still contactable once its consent requirement is met), but never a BAR, a HOLD_UNTIL_DATE or a HOLD_UNTIL_REFRESH. If one appears here the status precedence and the disposition map have disagreed, which is a build-stopping bug. NOTE the converse is deliberately NOT asserted: an AFFIRMATIVE code on a BLOCKED_UNTIL or INELIGIBLE row is correct and informative -- it says a valid consent exists AND a time window binds, which is exactly what a business reader needs to see to know the record becomes contactable rather than never.
